newsitem.title: USA: US STOCKPILE TABLES NEGOTIATED COBALT BID FOR FY97.
newsitem.headline: US STOCKPILE TABLES NEGOTIATED COBALT BID FOR FY97.

text.p: U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center tabled negotiated sales of coablt for the remainder of the fiscal year ending Sept 30, and will sell 500,000 lbs in a final sealed bid at a yet unspecified date, a stockpile official confirmed Tuesday.
A draft solicitation for the negotiated sale to be held Aug 29 was issued in late July, but is now off the table for the rest of the year, said Essie Schloss, general counsel for Stockpile.
If the sale goes as planned, Stockpile will have sold 2.3 million lbs as opposed to the 6 million lbs allocated for sale in fiscal 1997.

Stockpile's cobalt sales have been steeped in controversey, with the launching of a new sales method in which the many of the terms of sale are negotiated between the government and the bidder and not publicly disclosed.
Previously, all sales were conducted through a sealed bid approach, in which the terms are determined ahead of time by the government and the bids are public.

This year, Minor Metals Inc launched two lawsuits against the government's sales process, resulting in an injunction that prevented the Stockpile from selling cobalt from April to July and calling into question the negotiated bid process.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
